thread:
alyssa: Heads-up: saw a perf regression when we moved kvcache -> striped shards across TP+PP on the 8xA100 cluster. Baseline (replicated DP) was ~48ms/step, after stripe+tp it jumped to ~72ms.

alyssa: quick profile dump attached below (short). main smells: all-reduce spikes, lower vram-locality on hot rows, and kernel fallback to generic gemm on some quant paths.

alyssa: ```
step_avg_ms: 72.3
compute_ms: 40.2
allreduce_ms: 12.8
kvcache_fetch_ms_per_gpu: 6.1
overlap_pct: 28
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
kernel: fused_attention_qkv_small_seq -> fallback_gemm for heads 8-12
```

kevin: hmm. do we have nccl timelines? sounds like all-reduce isn't chunked and is blocking. any NCCL envs set (ALG_CHUNK or NCCL_COLLNET)?

alyssa: NCCL 2.12, default coll config. no collnet. I ran nvprof snapshot, attaching flame: allreduce on grad sync dominates ~30% during decode window.

tariq: if kvcache is striped across TP shards we get more inter-GPU fetches per token — that increases small-message all-to-all chatter. suggest trying two experiments: 1) affinity striping (group hot keys to same TP shard) 2) chunked all-reduce / async op to overlap more. also consider switching batching heuristic to microbatches when kv_hit_rate < 0.7.

kevin: +1 on affinity. also try NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL — might change path selection. For kernel fallback, can you paste the op meta that forced fallback? maybe fused kernel didn't support that sequence length/heads combo.

alyssa: pasted sample op meta: ```op: attention_fused
seq_len: 2048
heads: 12
dtype: int8
quant_mode: per_channel
available_kernel: fused_attention_qkv_small_seq (seq<=1024), fallback_gemm_quant
```

sreana: related: we saw a similar regression during the Llama2 sweep when we enabled TP across model parallel; we ended up adding a kernel-selector rule: prefer quant-friendly kernels only if seq_len<=1024 OR hot_key_locality>=0.8. that reduced regressions.

benchmark-bot: ablation run started (shard-stripe vs replicated, 8 gpus, tp=2 pp=2 dp=2). will post numbers.

benchmark-bot: ablation results:
- replicated (DP): 48.1ms/step, p99 110ms
- stripe-shard naive: 72.3ms/step, p99 205ms
- stripe+affinity heuristic: 54.7ms/step, p99 130ms
- stripe+affinity+chunked-nccl: 50.9ms/step, p99 118ms
(throughput measured on decode-heavy workload, kv_hit_rate ~0.62)

tariq: that looks promising. affinity alone buys most of it. chunked-nccl finishes the rest. can we codify affinity as: place top-20% hottest keys into the same TP shard, rest round-robin? also tie batching heuristic: if kv_hit_rate<0.7 -> microbatch_size = max(1, floor(request_len/4)).

alyssa: implemented a PoC patch: runtime/shard_manager: add policy "hot-affinity" + selector in kernel_picker to avoid quant-kernel on seq>1024. quick numbers locally: 72 -> 56 -> 51ms when combined. pushing PR now: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/4281

kevin: nice. please include perf test matrix and NCCL env knobs you tried in the PR. also add unit that simulates skewed hot-key distribution so we don't regress later.

alyssa: will do. plan: roll to staging with stripe+affinity+nccl-chunk flags, run full regression suite tomorrow morning, if green schedule peer review.

tariq: FYI, we should also add a lightweight runtime metric: kvcache_remote_fetch_ratio per request, to trigger adaptive batching at runtime.

alyssa: added a TODO in the PR for that metric. thanks all. :thumbsup:

kevin: great thread. follow-up meeting with kernel team and nccl expert? next wed?

alyssa: yeah let's sync w/ kernel + infra. I'll DM calendar invites after the staging run.
